finding.statement: The 'at most two gamma-images' exceptional locus of ATT-0083 clause (F) is controlled exactly, not just bounded: Gamma <= D_a+D_b forces D_a+D_b = Gamma + R with R effective of degree 2 in the class 3D-K = 2D-L, and h^0(3D-K)<=1 on a non-hyperelliptic fibre (degree 2 with two sections would be a g^1_2) makes R unique when it exists. Consequently {a,b} must contain gamma(supp R), so the locus is EMPTY whenever 3D-K is non-effective (the generic situation), is finite when the two points of R have distinct gamma-images, and attains dimension 1 only in the residual case where R lies inside a single gamma-fibre. This is strictly sharper than 'dimension at most 1' and shows the trivial-stabilizer locus is generically all of |L_b|^dist, which is what a later stabilizer or orbifold-cohomology computation on Z_ev would actually need.
